feature: Every tool that makes something hands back to Select
summary: Finish a path with the Pen and you are holding the pointer with that path picked, so the arrow keys move it and the panels describe it without a trip to the tool bar. The Pen was the last tool in the app that did not do this.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The Pen and path reshaping are on by default in Next; nothing new to switch on.

try.do: Press P, then click three corners and click the first one again to close the shape.
Look at the tool bar: the pointer is in hand, not the Pen, and the shape is picked.
Press the right arrow key four times without touching anything else, and watch the shape move.
Press P and draw a second shape the same way. One press of P per shape.
Press ⌘Z once and check the whole second shape goes in a single step.
Press P again while the first shape is picked: the Pen comes back and the shape's points stay on it, ready to drag.

evaluate: After closing a shape, does the pointer coming back feel like the drawing finished, or like the tool was taken off you?
Drawing an icon of five or six shapes: is one press of P per shape an acceptable price for the ending being the same as every other tool's?
Is the shape being picked the moment it lands what you want, or would you rather it landed with nothing picked?
Pressing P over a shape you already drew keeps it picked and shows its points. Is that the way you would reach for its anchors?
Does undo after drawing take back the right amount in one press?
rough: No pictures with this one: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole task, so macOS refuses every screen capture and a walk will not even run. The walks below were written and updated but not executed, and a sweep has been asked for so they run as soon as the screen is unlocked.

This reverses a decision that was taken on purpose two days ago. The Pen was made to keep itself in hand because an icon is five or six shapes in a row; that reasoning was real, and what beat it was consistency across eleven tools plus the user hitting the inconsistency twice. If drawing a run of shapes now feels slow, the thing to argue about is whether the Pen should be the app's one exception, not whether the hand-back works.

Picking the Pen up now keeps whatever layer was picked, where before it dropped it. That is what makes pressing P over a finished shape reach its points. The side effect is that picking the Pen up with a rectangle selected leaves the rectangle selected, invisibly: its handles are hidden under the Pen, and the first anchor of a new path lets it go.

The walk proves the arrow keys acted on the shape by undoing one step and checking the shape is still there, rather than by claiming a pixel position. A walk cannot read a layer's X and Y, so a nudge can only be shown indirectly. Step four of the try list above is the direct version, by eye.
